newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy ends mixed on exports, May tops $9.00/bu.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy ends mixed on exports, May tops $9.00/bu.

text.p: CBOT May soybeans topped the $9.00 per bushel mark for the first time since the 1988 drought but soybeans closed mixed after USDA weekly export inspections came in below trade expectations, traders said.
"The need to ration demand was the central issue going into the rally," said Mark Weidner, oilseeds analyst with Cargill Investor Services.
"When we had inspections numbers that questioned if we've actually rationed demand, that took some of the wind out of the sails. But one inspection number doesn't confirm the sales are slowing down."
USDA put export inspections at 5.988 million bushels, well below trade expectations for 10 million to 14 million bushels.
Weidner and others said old crop July fell in a knee-jerk reaction to the surprisingly low numbers but recovered on ideas this week's figure was an abberation.
Trade sources cited talk Thursday's USDA weekly sales figure would come in above 400,000 tonnes.
Soybeans ended 5-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 2-1/2 cents lower with July up four at $8.89-1/2.
The new high for the May contract is $9.02 per bushel, topping the previous high of $8.98-1/2 set on Friday.
